title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery
subtitle: ERAS colorectal bundle: compliance is the intervention

sources.title: Guidelines for perioperative care in elective colorectal surgery: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) Society recommendations 2018

red_flags.text: A patient falling off the pathway: not tolerating diet, not mobilising, rising pain or rising heart rate. This is a complication until shown otherwise, not an ERAS failure.
Discharge criteria met on paper while the patient still has tachycardia, rising inflammatory markers or new pain.
Unrecognised malnutrition or anaemia at pre-assessment, which ERAS elements cannot overcome on the day.
Low pathway compliance on audit: outcomes track compliance with the bundle, not the existence of a protocol.

do_now.text: Pre-admission: counselling and written information about the pathway, the expected length of stay and the patient's role.
Pre-admission optimisation: smoking and alcohol cessation, correction of anaemia, and nutritional screening with supplementation where malnourished; prehabilitation where available.
Fasting: clear fluids up to 2 hours and solids up to 6 hours before induction, with pre-operative oral carbohydrate loading in non-diabetic patients.

assess.text: Risk of post-operative nausea and vomiting, to plan multimodal prophylaxis.
Obstructive sleep apnoea and frailty, which change opioid and monitoring decisions.
Daily review against the pathway milestones: diet, mobility, catheter, drains, analgesia and discharge criteria.

investigate.text: Haemoglobin and iron studies early enough to treat iron deficiency before surgery.
Audit compliance with each ERAS element prospectively; the ERAS Society interactive audit system or a local equivalent.

resuscitate.text: Intra-operative: antimicrobial prophylaxis and skin preparation, standardised anaesthesia with short-acting agents, and multimodal PONV prophylaxis.
Minimally invasive surgery where expertise allows.
Avoid fluid overload: a near-zero fluid balance approach, with goal-directed therapy for high-risk patients.
Maintain normothermia with active warming throughout.

Mechanical bowel preparation alone should not be used routinely for colonic surgery; mechanical preparation combined with oral antibiotics may be considered. Preparation is usually used before rectal surgery.

definitive.text: No routine nasogastric tube, and no routine abdominal drains after colonic surgery.
Multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia: regular paracetamol and NSAIDs where appropriate, with regional techniques suited to the approach.
Early oral intake, usually within 24 hours, and early mobilisation from the day of surgery.
Early removal of the urinary catheter, usually within 24 hours after colonic surgery.
Prevent ileus: avoid fluid overload, minimise opioids, and consider chewing gum.
Glycaemic control and thromboprophylaxis, including extended prophylaxis after major cancer surgery.

escalate.text: Senior review when a patient deviates from the pathway milestones; deviation is often the first sign of a complication.
Dietitian for malnourished patients before and after surgery.
An ERAS lead or coordinator who owns audit and feedback; compliance falls without one.

notes: ERAS is a bundle. The individual elements have modest effects; consistent delivery of most of them is what shortens stay and reduces complications.
Early discharge is the result of recovery, not its target. A patient who misses a milestone needs examining, not chasing.
The elements that matter most are the ones easiest to drop: carbohydrate loading, avoiding fluid overload, early catheter removal and getting out of bed on day zero.
